Motivation
Kafka now uses "features" to declare the capabilities it supports. Features are versioned to evolve over time. The initial versions are set when formatting and can be updated at runtime via the UpdateFeatures API.
Brokers support a range of versions for each feature, and at a single time there is a finalized version that indicates the current version in use. The finalized version for each feature is a cluster-wide state: when upgrading or downgrading a feature, all brokers have to support it. Each broker reports the ranges it supports as well as the finalized versions. This is exposed via the Admin API.
Another version that is less visible is the "default" version of each feature for a specificmetadata.version. It is also a cluster-wide state. This is what is picked when formatting a node, or when finalizing an upgrade viabin/kafka-features.sh upgradewith the--release-versionflag. The default version is also by convention what is used in documentation, i.e. "feature X is at version Y in Kafka Z", "move to Kafka version Z for feature X". Not every feature has a default:metadata.versionis the input, andkraft.versiondepends on how the quorum was formatted rather than onmetadata.version.
Lack of Admin API support
At the moment, default versions cannot be retrieved using public APIs. They can only be retrieved using thekafka-features.shtool with theversion-mappingflag. That command computes the mapping locally using theFeatureclass from theserver-commonmodule. In addition, it requires running the tool with the same version as the broker to retrieve valid values.
Unable to reset values
Another issue that appears when defaults are unknown is that it is not possible to reset a feature to its default. Even with the default known, the client has to read the finalized version, decide whether the change is an upgrade or a downgrade, and send an explicit version; ifmetadata.versionchanges in between, the version it computed is stale. There is also no way to say "setmetadata.versionto X and all other features to their defaults for X" in a single atomic request, which is what finalizing an upgrade means. Today this is only available viakafka-features.sh upgrade --release-version, which computes the versions locally from the server classes.
No results from UpdateFeatures
UpdateFeaturesResponsedoes not contain the applied version for each feature; it only reports whether the request succeeded. A caller cannot tell whether a feature was changed or was already at the requested version (kafka-features.shprints "was upgraded to 1" for features already at 1). With a reset this gets worse: the caller does not know which version the controller resolved, and avalidateOnlyrequest cannot report what would happen. Version 2 of the response removed the per-feature results because they only carried errors, which became redundant once updates were made atomic (KIP-1022); they did not carry the resulting version.
